groups.statement: The library system administration module shall support staff management of configuration.
The library system administration module shall support staff management of users.
The library system administration module shall support staff monitoring.
The library system administration module shall support staff management of updates.
The library system administration module shall support staff management of backups without interrupting service.
The library operations and administration team is responsible for keeping the system running across all branches.
The central administration module shall support system administrators in managing the platform reliably and safely.
The system shall support backups and updates being handled on scheduled maintenance windows.
The system shall provide audit logging to track who changed what and when.
The system shall send alerts or notifications when something critical fails or an update does not complete.
The system shall assign permissions based on staff roles instead of requiring manual access configuration for each user.
The system shall support different access levels for IT users, branch supervisors, and other administrative users.
The system shall limit sensitive functions to authorized users only.
The system shall make it easy to review who has access to what.
The system shall support access review when staff change roles or leave.
IT staff shall have the highest level of access.
Branch supervisors shall have more limited access than IT staff.
Branch supervisors shall be able to handle some local settings if allowed.
Branch supervisors shall be able to report issues.
Branch supervisors shall not be able to change core system settings.
Administrative user roles should be customizable rather than fixed, if possible.
When a person changes roles, the system shall update their access immediately so they retain only the permissions associated with the new role.
When a person leaves the organization, the system shall disable or remove the account promptly.
The system shall log account changes for later review.
The role and permission model shall be customizable by administrators.
The administrator-customizable role and permission model shall include sensible guardrails.
The role and permission model shall support slight variations for different branches or operational needs.
The system shall not be locked into rigid predefined roles.
The system shall prevent users from creating overly broad permissions that could create security problems.
The system should support stronger authentication for higher-privilege accounts if feasible.
The system should make it easy to review inactive or stale accounts.
The system should provide clear visibility and quick administration so that access stays aligned with staff responsibilities.
The monitoring system shall provide a clear view of the health of servers, databases, applications, services, and interfaces between systems.
The alerting system shall notify staff quickly when something is failing, trending toward failure, or not responding.
The alerting system shall enable staff to act before issues affect library service.
The system shall help staff distinguish between minor issues and problems requiring immediate attention.
The system shall generate alerts for high CPU usage.
The system shall generate alerts for high memory usage.
The system shall generate alerts for low disk space.
The system shall generate alerts for service outages.
The system shall generate alerts for database connection failures.
The system shall generate alerts for failed jobs.
The system shall generate alerts for broken integrations.
The system shall generate alerts for interface errors.
The system shall support warning thresholds before conditions become critical.
The system shall allow alert thresholds to be tuned over time based on normal operating conditions in the environment.
Critical alerts shall be sent immediately to on-duty IT staff through channels they actively monitor, such as email or text if available.
If a critical issue is not acknowledged within a reasonable time, the alert shall escalate to a supervisor or higher-level support.
The alerting mechanism shall be reliable enough that users trust it.
The alerting mechanism shall not be so noisy that users start ignoring it.
For everyday use, the dashboard shall be simple and show overall status at a glance.
For everyday use, the dashboard shall indicate whether key systems are healthy, warning, or down.
For troubleshooting, staff shall be able to drill into more detailed information.
For troubleshooting, the detailed view shall include logs, recent events, and component-level status.
The transition between everyday-use and troubleshooting views shall be straightforward and shall not force users into separate tools.
The system shall protect against data loss.
The system shall protect against accidental changes.
The system shall protect against system failures.
The system shall allow operations to be restored as quickly as possible when something goes wrong.
The system shall back up important operational data.
The system shall back up configuration settings.
The system shall back up the system state needed to bring services back cleanly.
The system shall minimize downtime.
The system shall make recovery dependable.
The system shall avoid interrupting normal library service more than necessary during backup and recovery.
The acceptable data loss for operational data should be as close to zero as possible.

More critical systems or data shall have tighter backup schedules than less critical systems or data.

Lower-priority items shall not put core library operations at risk.
